items.stem: You ask Claude to summarise research and it returns a tidy summary with reference-style citations. What must you do before relying on them?

options.text: Check that each cited source exists and actually supports the claim
options.rationale: Correct: citations can be fabricated or mis-attributed and must be verified.

options.text: Assume they are correct because they are formatted like citations
options.rationale: Citation-like formatting is not evidence of a real source.

options.text: Delete the citations to keep the brief short
options.rationale: Removing attribution weakens the brief; verify instead.

options.text: Ask Claude whether it is confident

items.explanation: Correct: citations can be fabricated or mis-attributed and must be verified.

items.stem: Which TWO steps belong in a verification routine for a research brief? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Trace each figure back to its original source
options.rationale: Correct: tracing figures to their origin is core verification.

options.text: Label any claim that could not be confirmed
options.rationale: Correct: honest labelling of unconfirmed claims is part of verification.

options.text: Increase the length of the brief
Remove all caveats so the brief reads confidently

options.text: Present both figures, attribute each, and note the disagreement
options.rationale: Correct: honest synthesis surfaces conflict rather than hiding it.

options.text: Pick the one Claude wrote first
options.rationale: Order of generation is not a basis for selection.
